deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Grothendieck is studying an arrangement ('système') of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane. He wants to recover the cellular map ('carte') from purely combinatorial data, here called K^+ (presumably the incidence complex, with K^1 its 1-skeleton of vertices and segments). For each pseudo-line D he has a two-element set Ω(D), apparently its two orientations or sides. He has canonical isomorphisms φ_{s;D,D'}. When there is no monogon and no bigon, he defines Ω(s), for a vertex s, as the colimit (quotient) of the sets Ω(D) over the pseudo-lines D not passing through s. Ω(s) is then a 2-element set. He wants s ↦ Ω(s) to be a local system on K^1. For an edge with endpoints s, s', he picks a line D avoiding both and composes Ω(s) ≅ Ω(D) ≅ Ω(s'). Independence of the choice of D follows from axiom b).

This page opens with the parenthetical remark '(c'est = équivalent à b) !)'. So the independence of the transport from the choice of D is not merely implied by axiom b): it is equivalent to it.

He then states what remains to be done to finish reconstructing the map from K^+:
(i) Put a 'polygonal structure' on the set of arcs (half-edges) issuing from each vertex s. This means a cyclic order up to reversal, i.e. a dihedral structure on a 2ν(s)-element set.
(ii) Give a canonical bijection between Ω(s) and the two orientations of that polygonal structure. That amounts to choosing a cyclic orientation, i.e. a local rotation, at s.

In modern terms this is the passage from a graph plus a local system of rotation data to a combinatorial map in the Heffter–Edmonds–Ringel sense, i.e. a rotation system. Since the ambient surface is non-orientable, Ω is a non-trivial Z/2 local system on the 1-skeleton. It plays the role of the orientation double cover, with the sphere covering RP^2.

The next page carries this out. It identifies the oriented pseudo-lines through s with the arcs from s (2ν(s) of them). It defines a circular permutation ρ_{D→,s} for each oriented line D not through s, with ρ_{-D,s} = ρ_{D,s}^{-1} and with ρ_{D,s} and ρ_{D',s} equal or opposite. This realises the bijection between Ω(s) and the orientations of the polygonal structure.
errors: No mathematical error visible. The claimed equivalence '(= équivalent à b)' is plausible: independence of the transport Ω(s) ≅ Ω(s') from the auxiliary line D is a cocycle-type condition, which is essentially what b) encodes. However, b) itself is not shown on this page, so this cannot be fully checked.
The page states a programme rather than a proof. The construction of the polygonal structure and of the bijection with Ω(s) is deferred to the next page(s).

ideas.what: Defining a Z/2 local system Ω of local orientations on the 1-skeleton of a pseudo-line arrangement from line-indexed data, with transport along an edge via an auxiliary line avoiding both endpoints
ideas.modern_name: orientation local system / orientation double cover; chirotope sign consistency in rank-3 oriented matroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (orientation covers). For pseudo-line arrangements: Folkman–Lawrence (1978), Bland–Las Vergnas, Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences)

ideas.what: Reconstructing the map from a dihedral (polygonal) structure on the half-edges at each vertex, plus a choice of one of its two orientations in each Ω(s)
ideas.modern_name: rotation system / combinatorial map (Heffter–Edmonds–Ringel); cartes as in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heffter (1891), Edmonds (1960), Ringel, Tutte; maps/dessins: Grothendieck, Jones–Singerman, Cori
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) treats cartes combinatoires in general, though not this pseudo-line reconstruction

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short transitional page stating the remaining steps of a reconstruction: rotation system plus orientation local system. These are standard in topological graph theory and oriented-matroid theory. It is of mild interest as evidence of Grothendieck's local-system viewpoint on pseudo-line arrangements, but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads '(c'est = équivalent à b) !)', with 'équivalent' only partially legible. The machine reading is consistent with the image.
'{+finir de+}' is an interlinear insertion above 'reconstituer' (the word is plausibly 'reconstituer'). The intended phrase is 'Pour finir de reconstituer la carte à partir des K^+'.
The archive page number written at the bottom left is '66', whereas the catalogue gives this as page 63 of 69.
